National Register of Historic Places listings in Marion County, Indiana
Wikipedia GeoSearch, 3 km radius around downtown Indianapolis (39.7684, -86.1581)

stops.name: Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
stops.description: The 284-foot limestone shaft at the exact center of the city was the first American monument raised to the common soldier rather than to a general.

stops.name: Christ Church Cathedral
stops.description: Built in 1857 on the parish's original lot, this is the oldest church building still standing in Indianapolis and the only house of worship left on the Circle.

stops.name: Hilbert Circle Theatre
stops.description: Opened in 1916 as a deluxe movie palace, it has been the concert hall of the Indianapolis Symphony Orchestra since the 1980s.

stops.name: Indiana Statehouse
stops.description: Indiana's capitol packs the legislature, the governor and the state supreme court under one 1888 stained glass rotunda, and the public can walk in and look up.

stops.name: Indiana World War Memorial
stops.description: This mausoleum-shaped hulk anchors a five-block memorial plaza that Indianapolis laid out in the 1920s to court the new American Legion headquarters, and it worked.

stops.name: Central Library
stops.description: The 1917 Greek Doric library closes the north end of the memorial plaza, with a glass atrium bolted on behind it in 2007 that leaves the old facade untouched.

stops.name: Scottish Rite Cathedral
stops.description: A Tudor Gothic Masonic pile finished in 1929, its 212-foot tower carrying a 54-bell carillon that still rings over the north edge of downtown.

stops.name: Athenaeum (Das Deutsche Haus)
stops.description: Built as Das Deutsche Haus for the city's German gymnastic society, it is the best preserved building left from German American Indianapolis and still has a beer garden.

stops.name: James Whitcomb Riley Museum Home
stops.description: The Hoosier Poet spent his last 23 years boarding in this Lockerbie Square house, kept as a National Historic Landmark with his furnishings in place.

stops.name: Madam Walker Legacy Center
stops.description: Raised in 1927 by the company of America's first self-made female millionaire, this National Historic Landmark was the heart of Black Indiana Avenue and its jazz clubs.

stops.name: Eiteljorg Museum of American Indians and Western Art
stops.description: One of very few museums east of the Mississippi built for Native American and Western art, sitting in White River State Park in a sandstone building meant to read as the Southwest.

stops.name: Indianapolis Union Station
stops.description: The world's first union station opened here in 1853, and Amtrak's Cardinal still calls at the Romanesque headhouse three times a week each way.

stops.name: St. Elmo Steak House
stops.description: Serving in the Wholesale District since 1902, it is known nationally for a horseradish shrimp cocktail that reliably makes first-timers cry.

stops.name: Slippery Noodle Inn
stops.description: Indiana's oldest continuously operating bar, a blues room with two stages and bullet holes in the back wall from its rougher decades.

stops.name: Statue of Peyton Manning
stops.description: Nine feet of bronze outside Lucas Oil Stadium, unveiled in 2017 before a crowd of thousands, with Manning himself insisting he be sculpted wearing the helmet.

note: Indianapolis has never been scouted before; every other city run so far (Atlanta through Houston, alphabetically) has had a turn. All 15 stops sit inside a walkable downtown ring from Monument Circle out to Lucas Oil Stadium, roughly a mile end to end. Addresses came from the Center Township NRHP rows or from article infoboxes, never from coordinates; every ZIP was then looked up against the US Census geocoder, and the two the Census could not match cleanly (45 Monument Circle, 401 E Michigan St) were confirmed by name against Nominatim, which returned the Hilbert Circle Theatre and the Athenaeum at 46204. DROPPED: Indianapolis City Market, which is a fine 1886 building and a strong stop on paper, but it closed in March 2024 for a redevelopment not due to finish until 2027, so a player sent there today meets construction hoarding. Also passed over: Circle Tower and the dozen other downtown high rises the sweep turned up, since an office lobby is not somewhere to stand and be told a story. The Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument is the one stop with no house number; the NRHP row gives its address as Monument Circle flat, and I did not invent a 1.
